answer: Each new identity seals a unique 32 GB replica with Argon2id-keyed encoding bound to its public key, posting a Merkle root as its admission ticket. Verifiers then issue random 4 KB opening challenges every epoch with a 300 ms deadline, so remote fetching fails. Missed proofs forfeit a 40 token bond and revoke the ticket. A 10,000 identity swarm needs 320 TB of disk, about 30,000 GPU-hours of sealing, and roughly $19,000 upfront, plus 400,000 tokens at risk. Faking that depth resembles dumping ferrous ballast into a lagoon to mirror its bottom; every ton must really sit there.
